title: Event-driven order processing
problem: Accept orders quickly while isolating downstream processing failures, controlling retries, and preventing duplicate business effects.

requirements.availability: Order intake remains available during transient worker failure
requirements.security: Authenticated producers/consumers, encrypted queues, minimized payload data and auditable access
requirements.cost: Scale consumers with backlog and avoid permanently idle peak capacity

architecture.summary: API intake persists the accepted operation and publishes to an encrypted queue; idempotent consumers process with bounded retries and a dead-letter queue.

decisions: DLQ ownership and replay runbook are mandatory
Queue and data-store policies allow only named producers and consumers
At-least-once delivery is paired with idempotent effects and bounded retries
Consumer concurrency follows downstream capacity and backlog target
Event-driven consumers scale to demand rather than fixed peak
Batch operations where latency permits and remove redundant payload data

failure_modes.impact: Queue backlog and order completion latency increase
failure_modes.mitigation: Reduce concurrency, preserve messages and recover backlog within the SLO
failure_modes.prevention: Backpressure, downstream quota planning and load tests

failure_modes.impact: One operation cannot complete and may consume retry capacity
failure_modes.mitigation: Quarantine in DLQ, diagnose safely and replay only after correction
failure_modes.prevention: Schema validation, bounded retries and replay tooling

decisions.decision: Use an at-least-once queue and application idempotency key
decisions.trade_off: Additional state and expiry design prevents duplicate business effects
decisions.revisit_when: Ordering or exactly-once business requirements change

decisions.decision: Route exhausted retries to a DLQ
decisions.trade_off: Requires ownership and safe replay; prevents infinite retry loops
decisions.revisit_when: Failure classes or recovery automation change
